title: feat(#1157): show each role's emoji on its tmux and herdr tab, display-only
body:
## Context

The owner asked that each role's tab show its emoji with its name, so the tab bar tells roles apart at a glance. The `[identities]` emoji were used only in post signatures; no session adapter read them. Window names (tmux) and workspace labels (herdr) are the targeting identity, so the emoji must live in a display-only layer.

title: fix(#1290): route review dedup counts only this runtime's reviewer markers
body:
## Context

`mdstack route` dedups reviewer spawns against posted pass markers. It joined every review body on the PR and matched role/PR/head/round/pass with no check on who posted it. So review, validate or verdict markers from another runtime (another login, or the same login signed as another reviewer, as with `md-mt` signed Grok Bot on termproof) suppressed this runtime's own review and validation. The PR then sat with no local verdict until someone steered a rereview.

title: fix(#846): close-out closes a linked issue GitHub's auto-close left open
body:
## Context

When GitHub's auto-close misses, the merged-PR close-out leaves the linked issue open. #834→#765, #845→#839, #889→#860, #1022→#986 and #1029→#754 all merged with `closingIssuesReferences` set and the issues still OPEN, and the coordinator had to catch each one by hand (most were train lands). A landed issue left open reads as unfinished to dependents and was nearly rebuilt once (#860).

[Ash/triage] #1474: accepted → #1475

Root cause confirmed by Riley above: a builder's ad-hoc cleanup ran a bare `tmux kill-server` from a crew pane with `TMUX` inherited. Guard posted on #1440 and delivered to its builder (ack `20261109T035448Z-818fc4`). The structural fix is #1475 (`crew:ready`, M25.1, dispatched now). This card stays open until #1475 merges.

[Ash/triage] closed: root-cause fix merged

title: crew safety: a worker pane's bare tmux kill must not reach the crew server (#1474)
body:
## Problem

A builder's ad-hoc test cleanup ran a bare `tmux kill-server` from its crew pane with `TMUX` inherited, and killed the live crew server at 2026-11-09T03:16:42Z: every window died, and the owner had to restart the crew. Root cause and evidence: [Riley's finding on #1474](https://github.com/mw-ding/mdstack/issues/1474#issuecomment-6731802512). It's the #817 mechanism again. #817's sandbox shim and #1156's `scripts/run-tests.py` isolation each protect only calls that go through them, and neither covers an arbitrary shell command in a worker pane.

title: fix(#1475): a worker pane's bare tmux kill misses the crew server
body:
## Context

TL;DR: a bare `tmux kill-server` / `kill-session` / `kill-window` from a worker or lead window can no longer reach the crew's server. The tmux adapter now opens every role window with `TMUX=/dev/null/mdstack-worker,0,0`, a socket no server can listen on. Bare tmux calls follow `$TMUX` ahead of `TMUX_TMPDIR`, so they fail with `Not a directory`. The crew stays on the owner's default server: no dedicated or private crew socket, per the owner's direction ([#985 c6731966111](https://github.com/mw-ding/mdstack/issues/985#issuecomment-6731966111)). This is the mechanism behind #1474's outage, #1155 (folded in) and #817.

title: feat(#1053): owner-present caps under the session runtime
body:
## Context

The owner-present admission limits `present_builders` and `present_reviewers` were tmux-only, so a pack moving to `runtime.name = "session"` had to keep them in unchecked prose. This accepts both under `session` with the tmux meaning (default: the full cap), refuses a value above the full cap, and renders them in the session coordinator brief. tmux validation and admission are unchanged.
